why: The module's document buffer and the desktop's are the same EditableDocument, and the one thing that could quietly differ is the dispatch on top of it: which call an edit reaches, in what order, with which offsets. So every kind of edit is walked through one buffer here and the text after each is pinned. Both sides walk this file: the Rust test in src/tests/web_core.rs against the desktop's own buffer, and scripts/build-web.mjs against the built module. A step names its block by something the block's source contains and a splice by the text it lands after, so neither side carries a byte offset that a step above it would shift. Each document in `documents` is walked on its own buffer, in order.

documents.why: A workbook is the one document whose words are not in the buffer at all: every text cell takes its text from `xl/sharedStrings.xml` and holds an index into it, so what an edit rewrites is the cell element rather than any run of words. The buffer here is the sheet member, which is exactly what a package's buffer holds. Two cells share string 2, and the pinned text after the first step is what says the other one was left alone.
documents.source:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>
<worksheet xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/spreadsheetml/2006/main">
  <sheetData>
    <row r="1"><c r="A1" t="s"><v>0</v></c><c r="B1" t="s"><v>1</v></c></row>
    <row r="2"><c r="A2" s="1" t="s"><v>2</v></c><c r="B2" t="s"><v>2</v></c></row>
  </sheetData>
</worksheet>

steps.what: a shared-string cell rewritten to say its words inline, leaving the cell beside it pointing at the string they shared

</worksheet>
